nodes.description: External function delegatecall_selfdestruct(address _target) that performs an unrestricted delegatecall into an attacker-supplied target and returns the success flag.
Function parameter _target: caller-controlled address used as the delegatecall destination.

Unsafe low-level delegatecall to the untrusted address _target with selector bytes4(sha3("address)")) and this as argument, enabling arbitrary external code to execute in the contract's storage context (potential selfdestruct / storage corruption).
Named return variable _ans holding the boolean success flag produced by the delegatecall.

edges.reason: The function delegatecall_selfdestruct declares and receives the parameter _target in its signature.
The function body unconditionally executes the unsafe delegatecall operation on entry, with no access control or validation gate.
The caller-supplied parameter _target flows directly into the delegatecall destination, letting the caller choose the code that runs in this contract's context.
The boolean result of the delegatecall is assigned to the local return variable _ans and returned to the caller.

normalization_plan.reason: _target has no standalone semantic value; it is only consumed as the destination of the unsafe delegatecall and should be folded into that unsafe operation.
_ans is a purely local return slot of the function and does not carry independent security semantics; it should be folded into the enclosing function.
